{"id": "efc74f24-1423-4c9c-ac97-e1d1660ec06d", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "No — these should be treated as two separate incidents, not one.

I compared the `JobQueue` dimension on both alarms: one is scoped to `orders-queue`, the other to `billing-queue`. Since the dimensions differ, they shouldn't be linked or have one treated as primary for the other — even though they fired about a minute apart, share the same account/region, and draw from overlapping compute environments.

Shared infrastructure (same compute environments) isn't the same as a shared cause. Two job queues can stall for completely unrelated reasons — e.g., `orders-queue` could be stalled by a bad job definition while `billing-queue` is separately hitting a vCPU ceiling — and the close timing plus shared compute environment can make that look correlated when it isn't.

The right move is to schedule each as its own investigation, scoped to its respective queue. Want me to open investigations for both?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
